entities.name: Alexander II of Imereti
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alexander II, a pivotal figure of the Bagrationi dynasty, presided over the definitive fragmentation of the unified Georgian kingdom, establishing the independent Kingdom of Imereti in West Asia. Born at an unknown date, he died on April 11, 1510. His reign from 1484 to 1510, following a brief and contested claim to the Georgian throne in 1478, solidified Imereti's separate identity amidst intense internal strife and mounting external pressure from the nascent Ottoman and Safavid empires. His actions were critical in shaping the geopolitical landscape of the South Caucasus for centuries, marking a transition from a unified medieval Georgia to a collection of competing principalities.

Initially asserting himself as King of Georgia in 1478, Alexander II faced immediate opposition from Constantine II of Kartli and Kakheti, leading to the collapse of his claim over a unified realm. By 1484, he had retreated to his ancestral domain of Imereti, where he successfully established a distinct kingdom, ruling from the ancient capital of Kutaisi. His reign was characterized by continuous efforts to consolidate Imeretian power, including military campaigns against rival Georgian principalities and strategic alliances. He notably engaged in diplomatic overtures to European powers, seeking support against the encroaching Ottoman influence, though these efforts yielded limited tangible results.
